reason: The cited evidence confirms the lamellar L12/B2 microstructure (E1, E2) and the hardness difference between phases (E2). However, none of the cited passages provide direct evidence that phase boundaries act as dynamic obstacles, cause dislocation pile-up, or enhance back-stress under high strain rates; these mechanistic claims are unsupported by the cited data. E4 discusses strain rate sensitivity in a different single-phase HEA, not the eutectic system.
premises: Eutectic HEAs have lamellar L12/B2 microstructures with coherent interfaces
B2 phase is harder and less ductile than L12 phase
Phase boundaries act as obstacles to dislocation motion under high strain rate loading
Dislocation pile-up at boundaries enhances back-stress and yield strength
Higher phase boundary density increases dynamic yield strength and strain rate sensitivity
